consumer: An engine possession/eligibility check (e.g. a has_amount/charges_of-style on-person possession predicate as a mission or dialogue condition would use) asking 'does the avatar have >=30 rounds of 9mm on their person?'
scope: On-person possession aggregated across the avatar's carried items INCLUDING ammo contained inside magazines/guns/containers (charges_of('9mm') reach), not just top-level wielded/worn/inventory stacks
decisive_source: src/arcopolis_export.cpp::write_carried_items -- iterates only top-level u.wielded_items(), u.worn, and u.inv_const_slice() stacks and emits each item's own .charges, never recursing into it.contents nor invoking the engine's charges_of/has_amount possession aggregation; it dumps raw simulation-state (class S), forcing the consumer to re-derive the threshold
divergence: Avatar carries two 9mm magazines of 15 rounds each, each loaded inside a holstered/worn gun (or the rounds are inside a magazine inside a gun): the engine's on-person possession predicate returns >=30 (true), but summing charges over the emitted top-level carried_items finds 0 loose 9mm rounds and re-derives 'no'
